definitions.definition: A type of AI that creates new content such as text, images, music, and even code by learning patterns from assisted data, mimicking human creativity.
Large-scale AI models trained on vast amounts of data, capable of performing multiple tasks across different domains, unlike specialized models.
The art and science of writing prompts to improve the responses generated by foundation models.
A technique that allows foundation models to access and utilize private data to answer questions or perform tasks.
The process of adapting a foundation model to perform better on specific tasks or domains, applicable both in model creation and usage.
Applications built using foundation models that can perform tasks beyond just answering questions, such as booking hotels or managing schedules.
The operational aspects of deploying and managing large language model-based applications, including evaluation, improvement, and technical handling.
